expectation: Membrane rings on macrophages and DCs, often many CD14+ myeloid cells in stroma or at the tumour margin. In some tumours, sheets of tumour cell membranes. Weak on lymphocytes. How common it is varies a lot between cores and regions, and should not follow cell density.
observed: A: strength varies by core and region, with some cores bright across tumour-like areas and others nearly empty. B: membranous patches confined to some regions, with grain in between. C: sparse, a few blobs. D: a mesh of membrane outlines around dark nuclei. E3: some white overlap on CD14 cells, plus green outside them.
why: The signal follows regions, with membrane outlines and partial overlap with CD14, so it is a real population, but diffuse grain and background lower the contrast.
notes: PDL1 shows membrane-like rings and patches that differ by core and region, and partly overlaps CD14 cells in row E. Widespread grain and blobs off-target lower the contrast, so the stain looks real but weak.
